desc: The National Museum of Qatar in Doha surrounds the restored historic Palace of Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani (1880–1957), son of the founder of modern Qatar. The original national museum was founded in 1975; the new building by Jean Nouvel, based on the form of the desert rose and built of large interlocking disks, opened on 28 March 2019. The building covers about 52,000 m², and eleven permanent galleries form a 1.5 km route through Qatar’s history, natural environment and cultural change. Qatar submitted it to the UNESCO Tentative List on 2 April 2025 under criteria (iv) and (vi).
sig: Joins a historic royal palace and a landmark modern building to show Qatar’s shift from a traditional society to a modern state.
